# T112 — spend the card on training, not on discovering something does not work
## Why this exists

Operator, 2026-09-18: "I want a 100% utilisation of the 4090 today (I want it to be a meaningful increase on the LB rank) … make extensive plans and reverify the flow such that this does[n't] waste my resources tomorrow." And, mid-session: "2.5D CoAtNet at 224 — this guy is at 0.95."
The card arrives the morning of 2026-09-19.
The failure this task exists to prevent is not "we trained the wrong thing" — it is "we trained the right thing and could not score it."
## THE FINDING THAT WOULD HAVE COST THE DAY

src/coat_model.py's CoatMIL and the adopted notebook's RaptorClassifier are mathematically identical: same LayerNorm, same Sequential(Linear(F,256), Tanh, Dropout, Linear(256,12)), same clsW/clsb, same einsum('bkn,bkf->bnf'), backbones built with the same num_classes=0, in_chans=3, global_pool='avg'.

Every checkpoint we have ever trained for this arm would have been REFUSED by the pipeline that scores it — and the refusal would have landed at the end of an eight-hour Kaggle run, not at the start.

224 is 3.01× cheaper than 384 and 2.50× cheaper than 352 — and it is a legal size (224 = 32 × 7).
A correction this task had to make about its own claim. "336 is illegal" is true of res — the size the model sees — and false of img, the decode size.
Cell 47 groups arms by (img, slots, span, k_eval), decodes each group's studies once, and then resizes per arm to res inside eval_windows.
Their own dominant arm, maxspan-v5, decodes at img 336 — 32 × 10.5 — and is perfectly legal because only res reaches the backbone.
Two defects followed from conflating the two, both caught by a control and both fixed before anything was pushed:
The builder defaulted img to our resolution.
At 224 that opens a fourth decode group — one more full pass over the test set, against T105's measured 429–434 min and a registered 495-min cap, i.e. about 60 minutes of margin.
assert_decode_group_preserved() now refuses any img/k_eval that does not match the member being replaced.
The multiple-of-32 rule guarded img instead of res, so the builder refused to render a maxspan-v5 swap at all, with a message that was confidently wrong about why.

The registered configuration is therefore res = ours, img/slots/span/k_eval = the replaced member's. Our arm costs GPU passes only, never another decode, and the kernel's own [plan] N arms over M volume recipe(s) line must still report 3 — which is now asserted.
The operator's intel says a competitor is at 0.95 with a 2.5D CoAtNet at 224, which is our framing: our corpus is (N, 44, 336, 336) and our window is already three consecutive slices as RGB.
That intel is operator-supplied and unverified by us;
it is a reason to prefer 224, not a measurement.
T065 B1's "224 px is closed" does NOT bind here. It was registered against arm C / tf_efficientnet_b2 at 320, a different architecture on a different input path.
A pre-registered rule binds to its written scope.
4090 projection, labelled as a projection: the public trainer's author documents ~3.0 h for the full 384/bs8 16-epoch recipe on one 4090;
our laptop does 384/bs2 in 10.6 h, so the card is ~3.5×.
Applied to 224 that is ~1.0 h per 16-epoch fold.
scripts/t112/bringup_4090.sh measures it for real in 30 seconds before a single hour is committed — nothing downstream depends on the projection being right.

## THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING: scoring, not training
Submit-to-COMPLETE is 429–434 minutes — 7 h 09 m to 7 h 14 m (T105, measured against an HTTP Date header, not this machine's RTC).
Five submissions a day;
T057 rule 5 caps 3 structurally distinct.
So the day has at most two sequential read-then-act cycles:
push
scores
Training is no longer the bottleneck.
Scoring is. At ~1 h/fold the card can produce seven arms tomorrow and we can read at most two.
A plan that trains seven and scores two has not achieved 100% utilisation — it has achieved 30% and a pile of unscored checkpoints.
The consequence, and it is the whole plan: the 08:00 submission must be built from a checkpoint that already exists at 08:00.
The card cannot produce it — it will still be in its box.
So:

python scripts/coat_curve.py # the 224 fold python scripts/coat_curve.py --run outputs/t112/<tag>.json # any other
WHAT IS PLOTTED, AND WHY IT IS AUC AND NOT ACCURACY.
The competition metric is the mean of twelve column ROC-AUCs, and it is the only per-epoch figure a coat fold records: coat_train.py writes hist as (ep, loss, gold_auc, minutes).
There is no per-epoch accuracy to plot and no way to recover one -- only the argmax and the last checkpoint survive a fold, so epochs 0-15 cannot be re-scored under any other statistic.
Accuracy at the argmax is a number per label, not a curve, and scripts/roc_curves.py is the figure for per-label behaviour.
THE GUARD, in the idiom roc_curves.py uses.

A figure of a different run than the text beside it is worse than no figure, so this REFUSES rather than draws when the file disagrees with itself: best_gold_auc must be the maximum of hist, the recorded epoch count must match the history, and --expect (when given) must match the number the board and PROGRESS.md carry.
The drawn numbers are read from the run's own JSON, never retyped here.
WHAT THE FIGURE SAYS, on the 224 fold.

The metric climbs steeply to epoch 4, peaks at 0.8848 at epoch 7, and then drifts sideways-to-down for eight more epochs while the loss keeps falling monotonically to 0.632 -- the classic shape of a model that has stopped learning the target and started fitting the teacher's noise.
Half the fold's 3.5 hours bought nothing.

Every CoAtNet fold to date, this one included, trained with persistent_workers=True, which froze set_epoch in the workers -- so the per-epoch window resampling that coat_data.py calls "the augmentation" never happened, and the model saw ONE fixed draw of 12 of ~42 legal window centres for all 16 epochs.
A fixed augmented copy of the corpus is exactly the setup in which a model plateaus early and then overfits, so the flat tail is not safely readable as "16 epochs is too many".
